steps.say: Basal cell carcinoma is topping the skin cancer census. Nodular and superficial variants are behaving gently while aggressive infiltrating and morpheaform patterns are threading widely. Subtype is predicting the margin before the knife moves.
steps.tx: **Basal cell carcinoma** **BCC** (the commonest human skin cancer, from basal epidermal cells) is the most common human skin malignancy, categorised histologically into **nodular** (pearly rolled-edge papules), **superficial** (scaly patches), and aggressive **infiltrating**/**morpheaform** variants (scar-like plaques with wide threads). Subtype sets the margin.

vis.alt: Skin cross sections comparing nodular basal cell, keratinising squamous cell, and invasive melanoma.
vis.caption: Nodular BCC, keratinising SCC, and invasive melanoma side by side in skin section. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Small well-defined basal cell cancers are clearing with a four millimetre rim. A standard four millimetre margin is achieving ninety five percent histological clearance for low-risk primary disease. Recurrent or facial lesions are needing wider or Mohs surgery.
steps.tx: Standard surgical excision margin for low-risk primary **BCC** is **4** mm, yielding a **95%** complete histological clearance rate. Well-defined nodular trunk lesions suit this rule; morpheaform, recurrent, or midface lesions break it and need Mohs mapping instead. Trunk nodular lesions are the textbook case. This low-risk BCC margin rule covers trunk nodular lesions.

steps.say: Big, deep, nerve-hugging, or ugly squamous cancers are demanding wide rims. Diameter over two centimetres, depth past four millimetres, perineural invasion, or poor differentiation is marking high risk. Six to ten millimetre margins are covering the invisible spread.
steps.tx: High-risk cutaneous **squamous cell carcinoma** **cSCC** (keratinocyte cancer with metastatic potential) characterised by diameter over **2** cm, depth over **4** mm, **perineural invasion** (tumour tracking along nerves), or poorly differentiated histology requires **6** to **10** mm surgical margins. Microscopic fingers outrun the visible edge in all four settings.

**Mohs micrographic surgery** (mapped layer-by-layer excision with immediate microscopy) evaluates **100%** of peripheral and deep surgical **margins** via horizontal **frozen sections** (same-day microscope slices), maximising tissue preservation and cure rates in cosmetically sensitive facial zones. Clear layers stop the cutting; involved layers map the next pass.
steps.say: Every edge is being checked before closure in Mohs surgery. One hundred percent of peripheral and deep margins are being examined on horizontal frozen sections. Tissue is being spared and cure is being maximised where the face matters most.

Centimetres of surgery are following millimetres of depth. Five millimetres is clearing in situ disease, one centimetre is taking thin invasive melanoma, one to two centimetres is covering intermediate depth, and two centimetres is handling deep lesions. Breslow depth is dictating the ruler.
steps.tx: Cutaneous **melanoma** surgical excision **margins** (cuffs of normal skin) by **Breslow** depth (millimetre invasion thickness) are: melanoma in situ **5** mm, Breslow under **1.0** mm **1** cm, Breslow **1.01** to **2.0** mm **1** to **2** cm, and Breslow over **2.0** mm **2** cm. Millimetres of depth dictate centimetres of surgery. These melanoma margins scale with depth.

vis.alt: Composite clinical photos of melanoma with ABCDE features, nodular basal cell carcinoma, and squamous plaque.
vis.caption: Melanoma ABCDE lesion, nodular BCC with telangiectasia, and SCC plaque as seen in clinic. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Nodes are being sampled at eight-tenths of a millimetre and beyond. Sentinel biopsy is recommended from zero point eight millimetres up, and ulceration is pulling thinner lesions into the biopsy group. Thin non-ulcerated melanoma is being watched instead.
steps.tx: **Sentinel lymph node biopsy** **SLNB** (sampling the first draining node) stages melanomas **0.8** mm thick or more on **Breslow** measurement, and also stages thinner **ulcerated** lesions (surface breakdown promoting spread) under **0.8** mm. A positive node redirects prognosis and unlocks adjuvant treatment.

steps.say: One number is ruling melanoma prognosis. Breslow thickness measured from the granular layer to the deepest invasive cell is standing as the single most important histological factor. Every pathology report is leading with it.
steps.tx: **Breslow tumor thickness** (millimetres from the **granular cell layer**, the grainy epidermal stratum, to the deepest invasive tumour cell) is the single most important histological **prognostic** factor (survival predictor) in primary localised melanoma. Thickness stages, margins follow, and adjuvant decisions hinge on this one number.

vis.alt: Asymmetric brown lesion with irregular borders and colour variation showing melanoma ABCDE features.
vis.caption: Melanoma with asymmetry, border irregularity, and colour variation; excise by Breslow depth. Credit: Unknown author (public domain).

steps.say: Old scars and sinuses are turning malignant without warning. Marjolin ulcers are erupting as aggressive squamous cancers in burn scars, osteomyelitis tracts, and venous ulcers. Chronic inflammation is transforming, and these tumours are metastasising early.
steps.tx: **Marjolin ulcer** (scar carcinoma) is an aggressive **squamous cell carcinoma** arising within chronic non-healing **burn scars** (old burn contractures), chronic **osteomyelitis** sinus tracts (draining bone infection channels), or **venous stasis ulcers** (long-standing leg wounds). Suspect any rapidly changing chronic wound; these cancers metastasise early and need wide excision.

vis.caption: Marjolin ulcer: exophytic SCC erupting in a chronic scar needs wide excision and node assessment. Credit: Raj d0509 (public domain).
